_comment: 'As an additional cost to play this, you may charge your hero's soul. When this hits, if a yellow card was charged this way, this gets go again.' The shape is right: an optional CHARGE cost that stamps the charged card's colour, and an injected ON_HIT trigger gated on CHARGED_THIS_WAY yellow. The printed keyword is declared conditional rather than converted, because the condition is a HIT and there is no state for a static to read before the attack connects. The injected trigger now uses the NESTED form. In the string form the loader pops 'conditions' into an effect-level gate, so CHARGED_THIS_WAY was evaluated when the PLAY ability resolved and the trigger then fired unconditionally on any hit. Here that happened to give the right answer -- the charge is paid before the ability resolves, so the gate saw the truth -- but it was right by coincidence, and the same shape on rage_baiters was not. Since go again is stripped from this card by conditional_keywords, an injected trigger that fires when it should not is the difference between the printed card and a free extra action.
